test_cases.description: Verifies that both the secrets and variables tables exist in the SQLite database with the correct columns, types, constraints, and composite primary key.
preconditions: Hub database migrations have been applied to an in-memory SQLite database
No prior data exists in the database
test_cases.input: Query PRAGMA table_info('secrets') and PRAGMA table_info('variables') on the migrated database

expected.primary_key: Composite (owner_type, owner_id, key) on both tables
secrets_columns: owner_type TEXT NOT NULL CHECK IN ('user','org','workspace')

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: db = openInMemorySQLite(); applyMigrations(db); secretsCols = queryTableInfo(db, 'secrets'); variablesCols = queryTableInfo(db, 'variables'); assert secretsCols contains {name:'owner_type', type:'TEXT', notnull:1}; assert secretsCols contains {name:'owner_id', type:'TEXT', notnull:1}; assert secretsCols contains {name:'key', type:'TEXT', notnull:1}; assert secretsCols contains {name:'value', type:'TEXT', notnull:1}; assert secretsCols contains {name:'created_at', type:'TEXT', notnull:1}; assert secretsCols contains {name:'updated_at', type:'TEXT', notnull:1}; assert variablesCols == secretsCols; pkInfo = queryIndexList(db, 'secrets'); assert pkInfo includes composite PK on (owner_type, owner_id, key)

test_cases.description: Verifies that the store layer base64-encodes values before writing to the database and decodes them transparently on read.

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode:
store.CreateSecret(ctx, 'user', userID, 'MY_SECRET', 'hello world
line2'); rawInDB = db.QueryRow('SELECT value FROM secrets WHERE key=?', 'MY_SECRET').Scan(); assert rawInDB == base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString([]byte('hello world
line2')); vars = store.ListVariables(ctx, 'user', userID); assert vars[0].Value == 'hello world
line2'

test_cases.description: Verifies that no foreign key constraints exist on owner_id in the secrets and variables tables, and that cascading deletion is handled at the application layer.
preconditions: In-memory SQLite database with migrations applied
test_cases.input: Insert a row into secrets with owner_id referencing a non-existent user UUID

expected.note: Referential integrity is enforced at application layer only
expected.result: Insert succeeds without a foreign key constraint error

test_cases.assertion_pseudocode: db = openInMemorySQLite(); applyMigrations(db); err = db.Exec('INSERT INTO secrets (owner_type, owner_id, key, value, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)', 'user', 'nonexistent-uuid', 'KEY', base64('val'), now(), now()); assert err == nil; fkList = db.Query('PRAGMA foreign_key_list(secrets)'); assert fkList is empty

property_tests.description: For any secret stored in the secrets table, no API response body for GET, POST, PATCH, or DELETE on a secrets endpoint ever includes a value field.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random valid secrets (random alphanumeric keys, random byte values 0-262144 bytes) and create them via POST; then call GET list, PATCH, and DELETE on those secrets
property_tests.invariant_check: for each response body from any secrets endpoint: assert 'value' not in response_body and (for arrays) for each entry in response_body: assert 'value' not in entry

property_tests.description: For any raw value V of 0 to 262144 bytes submitted to any create or update endpoint, the value returned by a subsequent GET or PATCH response is byte-for-byte identical to V.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random byte slices of length 0 to 262144 (including edge cases: empty, 1 byte, 262144 bytes, binary data, multi-line strings, PEM-like content); create or update a variable with each value; then retrieve via GET list
property_tests.invariant_check: retrieved_value = find(GET_response.body, key=test_key).value; assert retrieved_value == original_raw_value (byte-for-byte comparison)

property_tests.description: For any (owner_type, owner_id) combination, the number of rows in the secrets or variables table never exceeds 100.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate sequences of POST requests (each with 1-10 entries) to the same scope until rejection; also attempt concurrent POSTs near the limit using goroutines
property_tests.invariant_check: after each POST (success or failure): count = db.QueryRow('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM secrets WHERE owner_type=? AND owner_id=?', ownerType, ownerID).Scan(); assert count <= 100

property_tests.description: For any pair of rows in the secrets or variables table with the same (owner_type, owner_id), no two rows have keys that are equal when compared case-insensitively.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random valid key names (alphanumeric+underscore, no leading digit, 1-255 chars) and attempt to create them via POST; include mixed-case variants of the same key
property_tests.invariant_check: rows = db.Query('SELECT key FROM secrets WHERE owner_type=? AND owner_id=?', ownerType, ownerID); lowerKeys = [k.lower() for k in rows]; assert len(lowerKeys) == len(set(lowerKeys))

property_tests.description: For any key K present at two or more tiers for a given workspace resolution, the resolved value is from the most specific tier (workspace > org > user) and the origin field reflects that tier.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random keys and values; seed them at all combinations of tiers (user only, org only, workspace only, user+org, user+workspace, org+workspace, all three); call GET /workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved for each combination
property_tests.invariant_check: for each key in resolved_response: if key exists at workspace tier: assert entry.value == workspace_value and entry.origin == 'workspace'; else if key exists at org tier: assert entry.value == org_value and entry.origin == 'org'; else: assert entry.value == user_value and entry.origin == 'user'

property_tests.description: For any response from any GET list or GET /workspaces/:slug/vars/resolved endpoint, the keys in the response array are sorted in ascending alphabetical order when compared case-insensitively.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random sets of 1-100 valid keys with mixed casing; create them via POST; call GET list and GET resolved endpoints
property_tests.invariant_check: keys = [entry.key for entry in response.body]; assert keys == sorted(keys, key=lambda k: k.lower())

property_tests.description: For any user, org, or workspace that is deleted, after the deletion transaction commits, no rows exist in the secrets or variables tables with an owner_id matching the deleted entity's identifier.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate random users/orgs/workspaces each with 0-50 secrets and 0-50 variables; delete each entity; query the database after deletion
property_tests.invariant_check: after store.DeleteEntity(ctx, entityID): secretCount = db.QueryRow('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM secrets WHERE owner_id=?', entityID).Scan(); varCount = db.QueryRow('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM variables WHERE owner_id=?', entityID).Scan(); assert secretCount == 0; assert varCount == 0

property_tests.description: For any POST request to any secrets or variables create endpoint, either all entries in the request are written atomically or none are; no partial writes occur regardless of which validation rule is violated.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate POST requests that fail at each validation stage (empty entries, invalid key, oversized value, intra-request duplicate, scope limit exceeded, cross-request duplicate); for each failure case, count rows before and after the request
property_tests.invariant_check: count_before = db.QueryRow('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM secrets WHERE owner_type=? AND owner_id=?', ownerType, ownerID).Scan(); resp = client.post(endpoint, body); if resp.status != 201: count_after = db.QueryRow('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM secrets WHERE owner_type=? AND owner_id=?', ownerType, ownerID).Scan(); assert count_after == count_before

edge_case_tests.description: Verifies that the store layer returns an error (not a garbled value) when a stored value is not valid base64 due to data corruption.
preconditions: In-memory SQLite database with migrations applied
A row in the variables table has been manually corrupted with a non-base64 value
edge_case_tests.input: Call store.ListVariables for the scope containing the corrupted row

expected.result: (nil, error) returned to the calling handler

edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: db.Exec('INSERT INTO variables (owner_type, owner_id, key, value, created_at, updated_at) VALUES (?,?,?,?,?,?)', 'user', userID, 'BAD_KEY', '!!!not-base64!!!', now(), now()); vars, err = store.ListVariables(ctx, 'user', userID); assert err != nil; assert vars == nil

edge_case_tests.description: Verifies that a failed database migration rolls back and returns a non-nil error, causing hub startup to abort.
preconditions: SQLite database is in a state where the migration will fail (e.g., table already exists with wrong schema)
edge_case_tests.input: Run migrations on a database with a pre-existing conflicting 'secrets' table

expected.result: Migration returns non-nil error; database is left in prior state; hub startup aborts

edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: db = openInMemorySQLite(); db.Exec('CREATE TABLE secrets (wrong_col TEXT)'); err = applyMigrations(db); assert err != nil; cols = queryTableInfo(db, 'secrets'); assert cols does not contain {name:'owner_type'}

edge_case_tests.description: Verifies that SQLite rolls back an uncommitted transaction on next startup, leaving both parent resource and its secrets/variables intact after a simulated crash.

Process crash is simulated after parent deletion SQL executes but before commit

expected.result: After database reopening, workspace and its secret both exist; no orphaned rows

edge_case_tests.assertion_pseudocode: db = openSQLiteFile('test.db'); applyMigrations(db); seedWorkspace(db, 'ws-slug'); seedSecret(db, 'workspace', 'ws-slug', 'MY_SECRET', 'val'); tx = db.Begin(); tx.Exec('DELETE FROM workspaces WHERE slug=?', 'ws-slug'); simulateCrash(tx); db2 = openSQLiteFile('test.db'); wsCount = db2.QueryRow('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM workspaces WHERE slug=?', 'ws-slug').Scan(); assert wsCount == 1; secretCount = db2.QueryRow('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM secrets WHERE owner_type=? AND owner_id=?', 'workspace', 'ws-slug').Scan(); assert secretCount == 1
